title: India Eyes US Trade Deal by July Though Challenges Remain
content: India and the US are keen to clinch an early trade deal before a July 9 deadline when higher US tariffs are set to kick in, but challenges remain, an Indian official familiar with the matter said.

title: SNB Rate Seen Stuck at Zero This Year After Last Week’s Cut
content: The Swiss National Bank probably won’t act this year on its threat of cutting borrowing costs to below zero, according to a majority of economists.

title: Hungary Is Set to Hold Interest Rates as Price Curbs Fall Short
content: Hungary’s central bank is likely to keep its key interest rate unchanged for a ninth month, holding steady amid mounting geopolitical risks and persistently high inflation expectations.

title: Japan’s Akazawa Says Still Working on Date for Next Trade Talks
content: Japan and the US are still working on setting the timing for the next round of cabinet-level trade talks, Japan’s point person for the negotiations said, as the deadline for a deal to avert another hike in tariffs nears.

title: South Korea’s Trade Chief Seeks Tariff Relief in First US Talks
content: South Korea reiterated its call to be exempted from US tariffs including duties affecting key industries such as cars and steel, Trade Minister Yeo Han-koo said after his first meeting with US counterparts since taking up his position.

title: Australia Must Choose Defense or Social Spending, Rabobank Says
Malaysia to Boost Venture Capital With Tax Incentives
content: Malaysia is dangling new tax incentives to investors to boost its venture capital industry, according to Second Finance Minister Amir Hamzah Azizan.

title: China Expands Its Coal Exports and Shrinks Imports Due to Glut
content: China’s coal glut is resulting in an increasing number of unwanted cargoes being offered abroad.

title: Korean Consumer Confidence Jumps to 4-Year High on Stimulus Hope
content: South Korea’s consumer confidence rose to the highest in four years as easing domestic political uncertainty, fresh fiscal stimulus and hopes for pro-growth policies under the new administration buoyed sentiment.

title: Canada’s Defense Pledges Mean More Borrowing, Watchdog Says
content: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s surprise announcement that Canada would spend 2% of gross domestic product on defense this fiscal year is a recipe for even deeper deficits, the parliamentary budget officer said.

title: UK Welcomes £40 Billion Amazon Investment Plan in Warehouses
content: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer welcomed a three-year program by Amazon.com Inc. to invest £40 billion ($54 billion) in the British economy over the next three years, including opening four new warehouses.

title: Trump Tariff Deadline Spurs Asia Export Surge, Wider Trade Gaps
content: The US trade deficit with Asia is widening as importers stock up ahead of President Donald Trump’s “reciprocal” tariffs deadline.

title: Federal Reserve to Eliminate Reputation Risk in Bank Exams
content: The Federal Reserve said Monday it will no longer consider reputation risk as part of its bank exams, following calls from some bank groups and Republican lawmakers to end a practice critics have viewed as unfair.

title: IMF Approves $1.3 Billion for Bangladesh as Reforms Advance
content: The International Monetary Fund’s executive board has approved a total of $1.3 billion in funding for Bangladesh as part of the ongoing loan program, as the South Asian country pushes ahead with currency and tax reforms.

title: Angola Gets Budget Relief From Oil Gains on Middle East Tension
content: Angola may meet its 2025 budget goals without major spending cuts if the oil price remains around $70 where it was benchmarked at, Minister of State for Economic Coordination Jose de Lima Massano said.

title: Argentina Economy Grows Less Than Expected as Imports Surge
content: Argentina’s economy grew less than expected in the first quarter of 2025 as a pickup in imports along with declines in exports and government spending tempered the South American nation’s recovery.

title: Goolsbee Says Fed Can Cut Rates If Tariff Inflation Doesn’t Come
content: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said the central bank could resume interest-rate cuts if the inflation hit from tariffs remains subdued, without weighing in on the exact timing of such a move.

title: Ireland Warns Thousands of Jobs at Risk From Pharma Tariffs
content: Ireland plans to use its budget cushion to pump money into infrastructure to protect competitiveness as global trade turmoil and tariffs threaten thousands of jobs in the multinational hub.

title: Fed’s Bowman Says ‘Time Has Come’ to Reform Key Capital Rule
content: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman warned the current approach to leverage ratio requirements has led to unintended consequences in the market while adding she could support lowering interest rates as soon as July.

title: BOE Chief Rejects Reform UK’s Plan to End Interest on Reserves
content: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said Reform UK’s plans to end interest payments on central bank reserves would do little to raise revenue and potentially slow down the pace of lending.

title: Nagel Says ECB Can’t Commit on Rates Given High Uncertainty
content: The European Central Bank shouldn’t commit to a certain interest-rate path, given how US trade policy and the situation in the Middle East are clouding the outlook, according to Governing Council member Joachim Nagel.

title: US Home Resales Stay Sluggish on Affordability Constraints
content: US previously owned home sales rose slightly in May to a still-sluggish pace that continues to show a housing market constrained by poor affordability.

title: Lagarde Reiterates ECB Well Placed But Monitoring Oil Swings
content: The European Central Bank is well placed to tackle “exceptionally high” uncertainty but will closely watch gyrations in commodities markets as tensions in the Middle East flare, President Christine Lagarde said.

title: US Manufacturing Expands While Inflation Measures Accelerate
content: US manufacturing grew at a steady pace so far in June, partly reflecting stronger employment growth, while two measures of inflation accelerated to the highest levels since July 2022.

title: Global Economy, Resilient to Tariffs, Faces New Mideast Storm
content: I’m Chris Anstey, an economics editor in Boston. Today we’re looking at the latest threat to wreck the global economic expansion. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Spain to Add Hurdles to BBVA’s Sabadell Bid, Vanguardia Says
content: Spain’s government is set to impose additional conditions on BBVA SA’s planned takeover of Banco Sabadell SA, La Vanguardia reported, in a further setback for the €14 billion ($16 billion) deal more than a year after it was first proposed.

title: Qantas Jet Takes 15-Hour Flight to Nowhere Due to Mideast Crisis
content: Passengers aboard a Paris-bound Qantas Airways Ltd. flight spent more than 15 hours in the air only to find themselves back where they started from in Australia after an Iranian missile attack shut down swathes of Middle East airspace.

title: Private Equity Firm Jadwa Said to Put Saudi Pharma Unit on Sale
content: Jadwa Investment Co. is looking to sell its stake in one of Saudi Arabia’s largest pharmaceutical groups, according to people familiar with the matter, offering buyers an opportunity to tap into a fast-growing segment of the kingdom’s economy.

title: Virgin Australia CEO Downplays Mideast Fears as Shares Debut
content: Virgin Australia Holdings Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Dave Emerson brushed away concerns the Middle East conflict will disrupt demand for travel as the airline surged on its return to the stock exchange in Sydney.

title: Bain’s Virgin Australia Rises 11% in Sydney After Relisting
content: Bain Capital’s Virgin Australia rose in Sydney trading after raising A$685 million ($444 million) in one of the country’s biggest initial public offerings of the year.

title: China On Target to Launch National Power Market by End of Year
content: China is on target to launch a unified national power trading market by the end of this year, according to its main electricity grid operator.

title: Apollo-Led Funds Invest $750 Million in Adani’s Mumbai Airport
content: Adani Group has raised around $750 million from global investors led by Apollo Global Management Inc. to refinance existing debt for India’s second largest airport.

title: Japan Bourse CEO Reappointed With Slimmer Vote as Rating Falls
content: Japan Exchange Group Inc. chief executive officer Hiromi Yamaji was re-elected with a smaller majority as his approval rating slid to the lowest ever and the bourse operator’s shares underperformed the market benchmark.

title: Nissan’s New CEO Faces Investor Grilling Over Job Cuts, Losses and Mounting Debt
content: Ivan Espinosa’s first annual meeting as Nissan Motor Co.’s chief executive officer was a baptism by fire, as shareholders questioned the feasibility of his turnaround plan and the carmaker’s failed tie-up with Honda Motor Co.

title: Chinese Port Activity Surges to Record After Trade Truce With US
content: Chinese ports just had their busiest week on record, likely due to exporters racing to get goods into the US as quickly as possible ahead of tariffs that may be imposed early next month.

title: South African Auto Firms Bracing for Tariffs Face Pay-Talks Test
content: A potential deadlock over pay increases for South Africa’s automotive sector workers risks shutting down an industry that accounts for more than a fifth of the nation’s manufacturing output, weighing on an already moribund economy.

title: Germany’s LNG Rush Benefits Neighbors as Storage Levels Lag
content: Germany’s liquefied natural gas terminals are busier than ever, but much of the fuel they import is flowing abroad — leaving domestic storage levels stubbornly low.

title: Nomura Shareholders Reject Proposal to Change Company Name
content: Nomura Holdings Inc. shareholders voted against a proposal to change the company’s name following a pair of scandals at Japan’s biggest brokerage.

title: Air India Cancels Europe, US East Coast Flights on Iran Crisis
content: Air India Ltd. suspended flights across major parts of its international network as the carrier, still reeling from a deadly plane crash earlier this month, joins major global airlines in grappling with extensive disruptions from the Middle East conflict.

title: China Expands Its Coal Exports and Shrinks Imports Due to Glut
content: China’s coal glut is resulting in an increasing number of unwanted cargoes being offered abroad.

title: Penfolds Maker Treasury Says Asia Leads Wine Consumption Growth
content: Treasury Wine Estates Ltd. said it’s seeing strong sales in Asia thanks to the reestablishment of its China market, and announced an imminent share buyback.

title: Starbucks Denies Plans of Full China Sale as Business Stalls
content: Starbucks Corp. said it’s not currently considering a full sale of its China business, disputing a report from Caixin Global that had sent the shares higher in late trading, as the coffee giant battles cheaper local rivals in its second-biggest market.

title: Star Trader Who Lost His Touch Bounces Back as Hedge Fund Coach
content: Danny Yong's pivot at Dymon Asia is beating returns at larger global peers.

title: Zopa Launches Current Accounts to Go Toe-to-Toe With Revolut
content: Digital lender Zopa Bank Ltd. is launching a UK bank account as it tries to compete with the likes of Chase UK, Revolut, and Monzo on everyday banking.

title: Hong Kong’s Smaller Developers Become $22 Billion Risk for Banks
content: While New World Development Co.’s mounting debt has captured market attention and shaken one of Asia’s wealthiest families, Hong Kong’s smaller property firms have lenders on even higher alert.

title: A $4 Billion Hong Kong Family Office Makes First Crypto Foray
content: A money manager to some of Hong Kong’s richest individuals will start investing in crypto, as more favorable regulations attract a wider array of investors to the digital-asset sector.

title: Tesla Robotaxi Incidents Draw Scrutiny From US Safety Agency
content: US auto safety regulators are looking into incidents where Tesla Inc.’s self-driving robotaxis appeared to violate traffic laws during the company’s first day offering paid rides in Austin.

title: Gulf States Reopen Airspace and Resume Flight Operations
content: Several Persian Gulf states, including Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, have reopened their airspace and resumed operations at some of the world’s busiest airports after halting flights as Iran launched air strikes at a US base in Qatar.

title: Tesla Shares Jump Most in Two Months on Robotaxi Rollout
content: Tesla Inc. shares climbed after the automaker rolled out its long-promised driverless taxi service to a handful of riders, a modest debut for what Elon Musk sees as a transformative new business line.

title: Northern Trust Commits to Staying Independent After BNY Approach
content: Northern Trust Corp. said it plans to remain a standalone company following an approach from Bank of New York Mellon Corp. about a possible merger.

title: Chewy Backer BC Partners Seeks to Raise $1 Billion in Block Trade
content: Funds advised by BC Partners are seeking to sell $1 billion worth of Chewy Inc. shares in a block trade.

title: Tiffany, Cartier Lost Diamond Rings to ‘Sleight-of-Hand’ Con Man
content: A man wanted by Interpol pleaded guilty Monday to stealing $260,000 in diamonds from Tiffany & Co. and Cartier last year through a series of “sleight-of-hand” tricks.

title: Bank of America Exits Consumer Regulator’s Monitoring Three Years Early
content: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau cut short a five-year agreement with Bank of America Corp. over the bank’s alleged submission of false mortgage data as the significantly curtailed government agency rolls back a bevy of settlements, ending the monitoring of BofA more than three years early.

title: Scotiabank Hires JPMorgan’s McDowell to Lead Corporate Banking
content: Bank of Nova Scotia hired JPMorgan Chase & Co. veteran Alton McDowell as global head of corporate banking.

title: Novo Exits Hims Partnership, Citing Concerns Over Compounded Drugs
content: Novo Nordisk A/S scrapped a partnership with Hims & Hers Health Inc. after less than two months, saying the US company is using “deceptive marketing” to sell copycat versions of its obesity blockbuster Wegovy.
